title: Co-Via: A Video Frame Interpolation Accelerator Exploiting Codec Information Reuse
problem: Video frame interpolation using DNNs achieves high quality but suffers from performance bottlenecks. Existing VFI acceleration approaches overlook temporal information embedded in compressed video bitstreams, missing a key optimization opportunity.
motivation: Real-time video frame interpolation requires efficient hardware acceleration, and leveraging codec information can significantly reduce computational burden and energy consumption.
method: Co-Via proposes a compressed VFI workflow that exploits codec information reuse to reduce DNN computation complexity. The FPGA and ASIC accelerators extract temporal information from compressed video bitstreams and use it to guide frame interpolation, reducing overall computation while alleviating hardware pressure through cross-layer codec-accelerator co-design.
key_novelty: Exploiting temporal information from compressed video codec bitstreams to reduce DNN computation complexity in video frame interpolation through cross-layer optimization.
contributions: Novel compressed VFI workflow leveraging codec information reuse
FPGA-based Co-Via accelerator achieving 10.31X speedup over RTX 4090 GPU
ASIC implementation with 2.4X higher throughput than state-of-the-art
Significant energy efficiency gains: 43.08X for FPGA, 3.6X for ASIC versus existing solutions
primary_theme: Hardware acceleration for codec-aware video processing
